extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners (practitioners involved in appeals and remands)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and substantive requirements for responding to an examiner's answer, substitute examiner’s answer, remands, requesting oral hearings, payment of appeal forwarding fees, and jurisdictional rules for appeals before the USPTO Board. Covers timing, content, and consequences of replies and reply briefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-month time period to reply to substitute examiner’s answer
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant must, within two months of the date of the substitute examiner's answer, exercise one of the prescribed options (reopen prosecution or maintain appeal) to avoid sua sponte dismissal as to the claims subject to the rejection for which the Board remanded the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two-month period is not extendable under 37 CFR 1.136(a). Extensions may be available under 37 CFR 1.136(b) (patent applications) or 37 CFR 1.550(c) (ex parte reexamination). If the reply is not timely filed, the appeal will be sua sponte dismissed as to the claims subject to the remanded rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant's two options after a substitute examiner’s answer (reopen prosecution or maintain appeal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant must either (i) request that prosecution be reopened by filing a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 (with or without amendment/affidavits/evidence), or (ii) request that the appeal be maintained by filing a reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment, affidavit, or other evidence filed with a reply brief will be treated as a request to reopen prosecution under 37 CFR 41.50(a)(2)(i) (i.e., treated as withdrawal of the appeal). Amendments/evidence submitted with a reply to reopen must be relevant to issues set forth in the remand or raised in the substitute examiner's answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for a reply to reopen prosecution (37 CFR 1.111 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply requesting reopening must address each ground of rejection set forth in the substitute examiner’s answer and comply with 37 CFR 1.111. The reply may include amendments, evidence, and/or arguments directed also to other claims or other rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reply is not fully responsive but is bona fide, the examiner should provide a time period to complete the reply pursuant to 37 CFR 1.135(c). If the reply is not bona fide (e.g., does not address the ground of rejection) and the two-month period has expired, the examiner must sua sponte dismiss the appeal as to the claims subject to the remanded rejection. Once a compliant reply under 1.111 is filed, the examiner must reopen prosecution and enter/consider the reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's treatment after a reply reopening prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: After appellant files a reply in compliance with 37 CFR 1.111 in response to a substitute examiner’s answer, the examiner must reopen prosecution by entering and considering the reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may make the next Office action final unless the examiner introduces a new ground of rejection that is neither necessitated by the applicant's amendment nor based on information submitted in an IDS filed during the 37 CFR 1.97(c) period with the proper fee. See MPEP § 706.07(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and entitlement for a reply brief (single reply brief rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant may file only a single reply brief to an examiner's answer within the later of two months from the examiner's answer or a decision refusing to grant a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 to designate a new ground of rejection in the examiner's answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions to file the reply brief may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136(b) (patent applications) or 1.550(c) (ex parte reexamination); extensions under 1.136(a) are not permitted. Normally appellant is not required to file a reply brief; if none filed the application will be forwarded to the Board for decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content restrictions for reply briefs (37 CFR 41.41(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply brief shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, or any new or non-admitted affidavit or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any argument raised in the reply brief that was not raised in the appeal brief, or that is not responsive to an argument raised in the examiner's answer (including any designated new ground), will not be considered by the Board for the present appeal unless good cause is shown. See 37 CFR 1.116 and 41.33 for rules governing amendments/affidavits/evidence filed after final action or after filing the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to timely reply (dismissal/cancellation)
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant fails to timely file a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 or a reply brief in response to a substitute examiner’s answer written in response to a Board remand under 37 CFR 41.50(a), the appeal will be sua sponte dismissed as to the claims subject to the remanded rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all claims under appeal are subject to the rejection, the entire appeal will be dismissed (application may be abandoned). If only some claims are subject, dismissal as to those claims authorizes cancellation of those claims and the appeal continues as to the remaining claims. The Board will prepare and mail the dismissal; examiner should follow MPEP § 1215 after dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal forwarding fee requirement (37 CFR 41.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant must pay the appeal forwarding fee set forth in 37 CFR 41.20(b)(4) within the later of two months from the examiner's answer or a decision refusing to grant a petition under 37 CFR 1.181.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to pay the appeal forwarding fee within the specified period results in dismissal of the appeal. The fee is premature if filed before mailing of the examiner's answer. The waiver of the appeal forwarding fee applies only where the appeal brief fee was paid before March 19, 2013; the fee does not apply to inter partes reexamination appeals. Suggested use of form PTO/AIA/34 for certification/transmittal; general authorization to charge fees is not sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting an oral hearing (37 CFR 41.47(b) procedure and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: An oral hearing should be requested only when necessary or desirable; if desired appellant must file a separate paper captioned 'REQUEST FOR ORAL HEARING' with the required fee within two months from the date of the examiner's answer or on the date of filing a reply brief, whichever is earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no timely request and fee are filed, the appeal will be assigned for decision on the briefs without an oral hearing. Form PTO/SB/32 may be used. Time period may only be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(b) or 1.550(c) (for reexamination). A non-compliant request triggers an Order for a Non-Compliant Request for Oral Hearing and requires filing a petition under 37 CFR 41.3 within 14 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing time limits and argument rules
rubrics_metrics.description: At an oral hearing, oral argument will ordinarily be limited to twenty minutes for appellant and fifteen minutes for the primary examiner unless otherwise ordered. Appellant argues first and may reserve time for rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the hearing, appellant may rely only on evidence previously entered and present argument relied upon in the brief or reply brief, except that upon showing good cause new argument based upon a recent relevant Board or Federal Court decision may be allowed. Demonstratives are neither required nor expected but may be used subject to submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrative exhibits and presentation rules for oral hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: If PowerPoint slides or other demonstratives are to be used, they must be submitted for inclusion into the record at least ten (10) days before the hearing date via USPTO Patent Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstratives must not include information not previously made of record in the proceeding; the Board will refuse demonstratives that do not comply. Parties must provide their own laptop for computer-based presentations and must clearly mark all demonstratives with the words 'DEMONSTRATIVE - NOT EVIDENCE' in the footer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public attendance and decorum at oral hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the public may attend oral hearings for appeals of reexamination proceedings, reissues, and published applications; members of the public are not permitted to attend appeals of non-published applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellants and attendees should observe hearing room decorum and business-appropriate attire. The Board's Oral Hearing Guide has additional rules and guidance available at the USPTO website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner participation in oral hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: If the primary examiner wishes to present oral argument, a request to present oral arguments must be set forth in a separate letter on form PTOL-90 using specified form paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must include PTOL-90 as a separate letter and email a copy to PTABHearings@uspto.gov after mailing to the applicant. If examiner participates, they will generally have 15 minutes to reply/present their position and may rely on arguments/evidence in the examiner’s answer, except new arguments based on recent relevant decisions may be permitted upon showing good cause. If appellant fails to appear, examiner typically will not participate unless panel deems it useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional transfer to and from the Board (37 CFR 41.35)
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurisdiction over the proceeding passes to the Board upon the filing of a reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41 or the expiration of the time to file such a reply brief, whichever is earlier; jurisdiction ends in specified circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board jurisdiction ends when: Director/Board remands; Board enters final decision; express abandonment under 1.138 recognized; an RCE under 1.114 is filed; appellant fails to take required action (per listed CFRs) and Board dismisses; appellant reopens prosecution pursuant to 41.40(b) or in response to a Board decision. Documents (e.g., IDS or petitions) filed while the Board has jurisdiction will be held in abeyance until jurisdiction ends. Board may administratively relinquish jurisdiction for file completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand authority and effects (Director/Board remands)
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the Director and the Board may remand a case to the examiner when necessary; remands are not appealable and transfer jurisdiction back to the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In absence of guidance in the remand order, the examiner should take action consistent with MPEP § 1207. Examples include remand to consider an IDS or to consider a reply brief; remand may require preparation of a substitute examiner’s answer and may require entering a new ground of rejection (e.g., due to change in law). See 37 CFR 41.35(c),(e) and 41.50(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute examiner’s answer for remand not for further consideration of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Board remands an application for a reason not for further consideration of a rejection (e.g., to consider an IDS, to consider a reply brief that raised new issues), the examiner may provide a substitute examiner’s answer and appellant may respond by filing a reply brief within two months from mailing of the substitute answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 41.50(a)(2) does not apply when the remand is not for further consideration of a rejection. Appellant cannot request that prosecution be reopened under 37 CFR 41.50(a)(2)(i) and is not required to reply to a substitute examiner’s answer written in response to such a remand. The Board normally will indicate whether 41.50(a)(2)(i) applies in the remand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply brief form/content requirements (identification and argument pages)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply brief filed to maintain the appeal should address each new ground of rejection set forth in the answer and should include specified items with each item starting on a separate page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply brief should include: (A) an identification page setting forth appellant’s name(s), application number, filing date, title of the invention, name of the examiner, art unit, and the title of the paper (Reply Brief); and (B) argument page(s). New or non-admitted affidavits and/or other evidence are not permitted in a reply brief. Any new amendment must be submitted in papers separate from the reply brief and are subject to 37 CFR 41.33 entry provisions; a paper containing an amendment is not a reply brief.
